user_stories.title: Create comprehensive PATTERNS.md documentation
acceptance_criteria: docs/PATTERNS.md file created with all 43 YAWL patterns documented
Each pattern has classification (KERNEL or DERIVED) per IDEAS.md specification
Each pattern has term form mapping (e.g., seq(TaskA, TaskB) for Sequence)
Each pattern lists semantic properties (e.g., 'XOR choice selects exactly one branch')
Each pattern has test coverage status (EUnit, property tests, validation)
All 43 patterns from WCP-01 through WCP-43 are included
Pattern module source files updated with -moduledoc annotations indicating classification
Documentation builds successfully without errors
Pattern registry (yawl_pattern_registry.erl) mappings remain consistent
user_stories.notes: This is the primary deliverable - the item.json explicitly requires 'Document mapping in docs/PATTERNS.md'. This documentation satisfies the 'kernel or derived patterns' constraint by classifying existing implementations, not rewriting them.

user_stories.title: Implement property-based tests for core control-flow patterns
acceptance_criteria: PropEr added to rebar.config test profile dependencies
test/yawl_patterns_properties_test.erl module created and compiles
At least 15 core patterns have property tests defined (minimum: all kernel patterns)
Property tests verify semantic invariants (e.g., 'exactly one branch selected' for XOR)
Property tests use PropEr generators for branches, tasks, conditions
Property tests run with minimum 100 iterations per property
All property tests pass: rebar3 proper succeeds
EUnit test wrappers created for running PropEr tests
Coverage report shows property tests supplement existing EUnit tests
user_stories.notes: Property-based testing is explicitly required by item.json: 'Include property-based tests where applicable'. Focus on kernel patterns first (Sequence, Parallel Split, Synchronization, Exclusive Choice, Join, Loop, Defer, Cancel, MI). Derive patterns can be deferred if time-constrained.

user_stories.title: Add property-based tests to individual pattern modules
acceptance_criteria: Each kernel pattern module includes PropEr tests under -ifdef(TEST) sections
Pattern-specific properties tested (e.g., sequence ordering, parallel branch count)
Properties use pattern state record definitions from module
Properties compile without warnings
Properties can be run standalone per module
At minimum: sequence, parallel_split, synchronization, exclusive_choice, discriminator, multiple_instances_sync
Pattern modules still compile without PropEr in production build
user_stories.notes: Adds module-level property tests for better organization. Must use -ifdef(TEST) to avoid PropEr dependency in production. Follow existing pattern module structure from PATTERN_IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md.

user_stories.title: Implement validation tests using bounded model checking
acceptance_criteria: test/yawl_patterns_validation_test.erl module created
Integration with existing yawl_model_checker.erl module
Tests verify soundness properties: option to complete, proper completion, no dead transitions
Bounded liveness test for deadlock detection (exploration depth up to 100)
All kernel patterns pass validation tests
Validation tests complete in reasonable time (< 5 minutes total)
Validation failures produce useful counterexamples
user_stories.notes: Validation provides formal verification of pattern correctness. Integrates with item 018 (validation backend). Focus on kernel patterns first - derived patterns inherit properties from kernel basis.

user_stories.title: Create performance benchmarks for pattern execution
acceptance_criteria: bench/yawl_patterns_microbench.erl module created
Benchmark 1: Sequence of 10k task steps (target: ≤ 10 μs/step)
Benchmark 2: Parallel split with 100 branches (target: ≤ 500 μs/branch)
Benchmark 3: Repeated discriminator pattern (target: ≤ 10ms/iteration)
Benchmarks measure and report timing (total time, per-operation time)
Performance targets documented in PATTERNS.md
All benchmarks meet targets within 20% tolerance
Benchmarks run successfully on reference hardware
user_stories.notes: Performance baseline for future optimization. Microbench approach matches IDEAS.md requirements. Use erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond) for accurate measurements. If targets missed, document findings and create follow-up item.

user_stories.title: Document performance characteristics in PATTERNS.md
acceptance_criteria: Performance characteristics section added to docs/PATTERNS.md
Benchmark results documented for all core patterns
Per-step overhead analysis included (Petri net, XES, OTel overhead)
Cancellation latency documented (activity, case, region)
Memory footprint estimates provided
Overhead scaling analysis (O(n), O(log n), etc.)
Performance data includes hardware configuration for reproducibility
user_stories.notes: Depends on US-005. Performance documentation helps users understand pattern costs and enables future optimization work. Include both absolute timings and relative scaling.
